nodes.title: CLIP Text Encode (Positive Prompt)
widgets_values:
Transform the input image into a polished stylized 3D anime render with clean stylized forms — keep real 3D volume and depth, not flat 2D, not photorealistic — while using the input image as a strict structural and spatial reference.

Preserve the subject's recognizable identity, exact object count, pose, expression, proportions, silhouette, orientation, size, position, camera viewpoint, perspective, framing, composition, occlusion relationships, and background layout. Preserve the original design and main semantic colors of the subject while allowing a controlled stylized anime color treatment.

Keep the background uniformly pure black (#000000), flat and completely featureless. Do not introduce scenery, a floor, a horizon, gradients, atmospheric effects, glow, reflections, cast shadows, particles, props, or environmental elements.

Render the existing subject as a stylized 3D anime render: keep clear 3D volume, smooth sculpted stylized forms, stable geometry, soft volumetric shading, and form depth — like a 3D animated film, not photorealistic and not flat. Simplify fine surface details and textures (avoid photorealistic skin pores, fur strands, or food micro-texture) but keep smooth 3D forms and soft shading. Apply soft clean lighting only to the subject without illuminating the black background. Stylize the subject's surface details. For subjects that naturally have a face (persons and animals), keep the face stylized in the 3D anime style without changing recognizable positions or proportions. For inanimate objects that do not have a face, do not add any face, eyes, mouth, nose, head, or human features — render them as plain stylized 3D objects.

Change only the rendering style, materials, shading, color treatment, surface texture, and minor internal details. Small local variations required to create a coherent 3D appearance are allowed, but the outer contour, major geometry, facial landmarks, clothing design, accessories, and object structure must remain consistent.

Do not transform the subject into an existing character or reproduce any recognizable character identity, costume, hairstyle, or accessories. Do not drastically exaggerate body proportions or alter object geometry. Subjects that naturally have a face may have stylized facial features; inanimate objects must not have any face, eyes, head, or human features. Do not add, remove, duplicate, merge, or replace any object. Do not change the pose, camera angle, perspective, framing, crop, zoom, rotation, or subject placement. Do not add text, logos, borders, or watermarks.
